payload.text: Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion. Agreed: no start time in ToolUse props, so measure around next(e) with the mod clock (it includes approval waits); ToolUse has no ctrl+o signal, so the raw view is the /tool-rows toggle; Bash has no numeric exit code and the error text has no guaranteed format, so parse it when present and else show no code. Corrections from the second opinion: quiet-items ready means initialized, not that it drew a row, so tool-rows must defer by the quiet-items row state of that call, not by the ready key; the Updated file diff placement inside ToolResult needs a live probe. Biggest risk: a short row hides output or a diff with false certainty. Second opinion: build Bash first inside tool-rows, with the engine row for every case it does not cover. Live probes still open: ctrl+o, bashEditDiff placement, exit code text, the clock redraw.

Design 2026-10-08: design lane plus Codex second opinion, both pick a new mod agent-board with its own Pane. Confirmed in the types: tool.call input carries the agentId of a subagent loop; agent.spawn fires for the Agent tool and resolves with an optional agentId; turn.complete carries durationMs and an optional usage; agent.list leaves out workflow agents and drops ended agents; no render component reaches the engine tasks list. Limits: two Panes do not show at once, they become tabs; agent.list history expires, so the mod keeps the rows it saw and marks lost history as unknown; forked-skill agents may appear without agent.spawn. Hot path: the tool.call hook passes main-loop calls straight through and keeps bounded memory per agent; list and render work runs only while the pane is shown. Live probes open: tool.call with agentId from a background subagent, agent.list retention, the hook cost.
